actions.action: Unpot parent plant and inspect roots and stems for rot
Cut away rotted tissue from parent with sterilized scissors
Re-cut every cutting above lesions with sterilized blade
Let cut ends dry/callus for 1-2 hours
Discard cuttings with no firm green tissue
Place cuttings in clean jar with fresh water in bright indirect light, no moss
Water parent only when top 2 inches of soil are dry
Repot parent into a pot with drainage hole if needed

reason: The answer diagnoses stem rot instead of the confirmed slow rooting caused by too-frequent water changes and moss; it does remove the moss but keeps frequent water changes and adds re-cutting, both of which work against the fix and can delay rooting.
